correctness.rationale: For all distinct nonzero ternary cubics F,G over F2, exhaustive projective point evaluation on the seven normalized vectors computes distinct rational intersections, while common geometric components are exactly those admitting a common F2 factor of degree one or two. The descent claim follows because the full Frobenius orbit of a geometric common irreducible factor divides both forms, and distinct degree-three F2 forms cannot share a degree-three factor. Independent direct enumeration over all 522753 unordered pairs of the 1023 nonzero forms and the complete seven linear/63 quadratic divisor-incidence table reproduces the unordered coprime histogram (69972,163191,162918,85554,23604,3339,210,0), hence the stated doubled ordered spectrum and maximum six. The source's separately inspected exhaustive PGL3(F2) substitution program enumerates all 168 matrices and obtains five nonoverlapping extremal orbits with sizes 84,28,28,28,42 and representatives (10,180),(10,660),(10,670),(16,446),(57,407). The independent count was complete; independent orbit enumeration was not separately rerun, so the orbit check rests on reconstructed exhaustive code and the total-size partition, not on a fresh second implementation.

The exact all-pair histogram, sharp six-point extremum instead of seven, and five extremal projective classes are natural finite-geometric invariants that can be reused as reference counts.
